articles.title: Pressure on landlord costs increase as Renters’ Rights Act looms
articles.summary: The average landlord is now carrying £714,000 in borrowing and paying around £25,000 a year in interest alone, before tax, maintenance or compliance costs are taken into account, according to new analysis from Pepper Money and Pegasus Insights.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords face mounting financial pressure, with an average debt of £714,000 and annual interest payments of £25,000, excluding other expenses.  
- The upcoming Renters’ Rights Act adds to the strain, prompting concerns over rising operational costs for property owners.

articles.title: Wave of last-minute instructions as landlords exit ahead of RRA
articles.summary: With the Renters’ Rights Act coming into force this Friday, Kent and London law firm Thackray Williams says it has had a wave of last-minute instructions from landlords looking to exit the market.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are scrambling to exit the market ahead of the Renters' Rights Act implementation this Friday, according to Kent and London law firm Thackray Williams.  
- The surge in last-minute instructions indicates widespread concern among landlords about the new regulations.

articles.title: Chief property ombudsman welcomes RRA but says landlords need support
articles.summary: The UK’s chief property ombudsman Lesley Horton has said she welcomes the reforms coming with the Renters’ Right Act implementation this week but says that small-scale landlords in particular will need support to adapt to the changes.
articles.ai_summary:
- Chief property ombudsman Lesley Horton praises the Renters’ Right Act reforms but urges for better support for small-scale landlords.  
- The impending implementation highlights the need for guidance to help landlords navigate the upcoming changes in the rental landscape.

articles.title: Nervous landlords prompt tenfold rise in instructions, says agent
articles.summary: North-east residential lettings agency Xenia Lettings says it has seen a tenfold rise in instructions from property owners since the start of 2026 as private landlords seek expert help to navigate the Renters’ Rights Act, the biggest phase of which goes live on Friday.
articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: Reeves reported to be considering rent controls
articles.summary: Chancellor Rachel Reeves is reported to be thinking about imposing rent controls on Private Rented Sector landlords as part of a range of measures to limit the impact of the Iran War on household finances.
articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: HMRC increases scrutiny of residential valuations
articles.summary: HMRC is increasingly challenging residential property valuations in inheritance tax (IHT) returns, with the number of cases referred to the Valuation Office Agency (VOA) rising 23.5% in the last year, according to research from TWM Solicitors, a private wealth and family law firm.
articles.ai_summary:
- HMRC is ramping up scrutiny on residential property valuations for inheritance tax returns, with referrals to the Valuation Office Agency up by 23.5% in just one year.
- Increased challenges signal a tightening approach from HMRC, as property owners face greater scrutiny over their valuation claims.

articles.title: Landlords urged to carry out more detailed pre-purchase checks after RRA

articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: Most landlords to be stricter choosing tenants – survey

articles.ai_summary:
- 25% of landlords are considering leaving the market due to the new Renters' Rights Act.  
- 60% of remaining landlords plan to tighten tenant vetting processes.

articles.title: Maintenance expert shares top Spring tips to cut costs

articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords can save costs this Spring by addressing winter-related maintenance issues and ensuring compliance with new responsibilities under the Renters' Rights Act.  
- Taking proactive maintenance steps now can prevent more expensive repairs down the line and enhance tenant satisfaction.

articles.title: Pressure on rents to continue despite halving house price growth forecast
articles.summary: Knight Frank has halved its near-term house price growth forecast to 1.5% for 2026 and lowered itsrental forecasts marginally, due to the economic impacts of conflict in the Middle East.
articles.ai_summary:
- Knight Frank has cut its house price growth forecast for 2026 to just 1.5%, reflecting economic uncertainties linked to the Middle East conflict.  
- Despite the revision in house prices, pressure on rents is expected to persist.

articles.title: Four in five landlords unprepared for Renters’ Right Act
articles.summary: Four in five landlords (82%) are concerned about the impact of the Renters’ Rights Act, with one in two (44%) very concerned. Meanwhile, three-quarters (75%) of landlords say regulation has made them less likely to grow their portfolios, and half (49%) are planning to sell or reduce their stake within two months.
articles.ai_summary:
- **Major Concern:** 82% of landlords are worried about the Renters' Rights Act, with 44% expressing strong anxiety about its implications.  
- **Market Impact:** 75% feel regulations deter portfolio growth, and nearly half (49%) plan to sell or downsize within two months.

articles.title: Energy efficiency and EPC ratings become higher focus for tenants
articles.summary: Landlords must consider how to improve EPC ratings to attract tenants, even ahead of the new requirement to upgrade rental properties to a C rating by 2030. It comes as energy efficiency of properties has gained even greater focus as tenants look to save money after the energy price hikes caused by the Iran War.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are urged to enhance EPC ratings to attract tenants, with new regulations mandating a minimum C rating by 2030.  
- Rising energy prices, attributed to the Iran War, have shifted tenant priorities toward energy-efficient properties for cost savings.

articles.ai_summary:

articles.title: Landlords warned a hidden leak could cost thousands
articles.summary: With more than half (58%) of hidden leaks originating outside a property, landlords must remember to focus on the maintenance of pipework outside as well as inside the property, leak detection specialist Aspect has warned.
articles.ai_summary:
- Over 58% of hidden leaks in properties start outdoors, emphasizing the need for landlords to maintain external pipework.
- Neglecting outside maintenance could lead to costly repairs, according to leak detection expert Aspect.

articles.title: As RRA deadline looms, 5 top tips for landlords
articles.summary: From 1 May 2026, the Renters’ Rights Act will implement some of the biggest changes to the Private Rented Sector in England and Wales. The Act will aim to balance landlord and tenant rights and will impose new requirements and regulatory oversight on landlords.
articles.ai_summary:
- Major reforms coming with the Renters’ Rights Act effective May 1, 2026, will reshape the Private Rented Sector in England and Wales, enhancing tenant protections while regulating landlords.
- Landlords are urged to prepare for the upcoming changes by following essential guidelines to ensure compliance with the new regulations.
